name: Antalya
title: Antalya Thickness Gauging | Cruise, Cargo and Yacht UTM
description: Ship thickness measurement in Antalya for cargo ships, cruise tenders, steel superyachts and workboats: UTM of hull, tanks and piping at berth or anchor.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships and Yachts at Antalya
intro: Antalya is better known for cruise calls and holidays than for heavy cargo, but its port still handles general cargo, bulk minerals and agricultural exports, and the coast around it supports a busy yacht and workboat trade. Atlantis technicians travel from India to the vessel. Gauging is planned around the port's seasonal pattern, berth stays and the lay-by time that yachts and smaller commercial ships spend alongside.

highlights.h: Cargo and cruise at one port
highlights.p: Antalya's main port handles general cargo and bulk alongside seasonal cruise calls, so a mobilisation can serve a coaster discharging minerals one day and a visiting vessel's tender or service craft the next.
The wider Antalya coast builds and refits yachts and workboats. Steel hulls and tanks on these vessels respond well to ultrasonic gauging, particularly before a refit or a sale.
Ships calling inside the Mediterranean ECA that burn high-sulphur fuel run exhaust gas cleaning systems whose wash-water and overboard piping benefit from regular wall-thickness checks.

port.h: Antalya: cruise harbour, cargo port and yacht coast
p: Antalya lies on the Gulf of Antalya on Turkey's Mediterranean coast, with the Taurus mountains close behind and a long tourist coastline stretching east and west. The commercial port, a few kilometres from the city, handles general cargo, bulk minerals and agricultural produce for export, along with a busy cruise terminal in season. The anchorage in the gulf is open to the south, so southerly swell can restrict launch work at times, though the sheltered berths inside the port are more reliable.

Ship traffic is varied rather than heavy. Coasters and small general cargo ships carry minerals, building materials and produce, occasional bulk carriers load or discharge, and cruise ships call through the season, sometimes with their own tenders and service craft working the harbour. Beyond the commercial port, marinas and yacht yards along the coast handle motor yachts and sailing vessels, some of which have steel or aluminium hulls that benefit from thickness checks before refit or sale. Antalya also sees ferries and passenger craft serving local routes.

For inspection, this variety means the gauging demand is distributed across several vessel types rather than concentrated in a single trade. Cargo ships need holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks checked, steel yachts need shell and tank plating measured, and cruise tenders and workboats need hull checks before service. There is no large ocean-going drydock at Antalya, so merchant ships needing a renewal survey generally go to the Marmara or to another Mediterranean yard, and readings taken here are used to plan that docking.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in and around Antalya
p: At the commercial port, cargo ships are gauged alongside during their stay. Holds are measured as discharge frees them, hatch covers and coamings are checked from the deck, and ballast tanks are entered once the crew have emptied and ventilated them and the master has issued the permit. Cruise ships offer very limited windows, so work there is restricted to tenders, service craft and defined spaces that the ship's technical team releases. Access is through the port's security procedures and arranged via the ship's agent.

Yachts and smaller commercial vessels are gauged at marinas, repair quays or on slipways along the coast, where the yard or marina sets the rules and the vessel can be supported or hauled out. A steel yacht with a hull survey in prospect can be measured over several days, including tanks and keel structure when accessible. For ships at anchor in the gulf, launches are arranged through the agent and used when the sea allows, with the most valuable readings taken first.
list: Antalya commercial port cargo berths — hold, hatch cover and coaming gauging on coasters and small bulk carriers during cargo work
Cruise terminal — hull and tank checks on tenders and service craft released by the ship's technical team
Anchorage in the Gulf of Antalya — deck and ballast tank gauging on ships waiting for orders or berth, by launch when conditions allow
Yacht yards and marinas along the coast — shell, tank and keel structure gauging on steel superyachts ahead of a refit or sale
Repair quays and slipways — hull plating and piping checks on workboats, ferries and fishing vessels hauled out or alongside

context.h: Port state control and Mediterranean emissions rules at Antalya
p: Turkey is covered by the Mediterranean MoU on port state control, and ship safety and ports are administered by the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure through the harbour masters. The cargo ships calling at Antalya are mostly smaller general cargo vessels whose structural condition varies, and recurring findings include wasted hatch covers, corroded coamings and deteriorated deck fittings. Cruise ships and large yachts have their own regulatory regimes, but the underlying question of hull steel condition remains the same for owners.

Antalya lies inside the Mediterranean sulphur emission control area, so ships burning high-sulphur fuel must run an exhaust gas cleaning system there, and the wash-water and overboard piping of those systems is a known source of thinning and leaks. Ships that go on to EU ports also face EU ETS reporting and, for those in scope, FuelEU Maritime obligations, and a valid Inventory of Hazardous Materials is required for ships calling at EU ports under the Ship Recycling Regulation. Owners often use the gauging results to support docking and refit decisions.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Antalya
jobs.p: Jobs at Antalya divide into commercial cargo work and yacht or workboat work. Coasters and small bulk carriers give hold and hatch access during discharge, steel yachts give long working windows in a yard or marina, and cruise tenders give a short set of defined checks. Owners are usually preparing for a survey, a refit, a charter delivery or a sale.
list: Hold, hatch cover and coaming gauging on a small bulk carrier discharging minerals at the port, ahead of an intermediate survey.
Ballast tank and deck gauging on a general cargo ship waiting at the gulf anchorage, with the readings organised by frame for the superintendent.
Shell, tank and keel structure gauging on a steel motor yacht in a coastal yard before a refit, to confirm which plates need renewal.
Hull checks on a cruise ship's tender at the cruise terminal, performed during a scheduled call and reported before the tender returned to service.
Exhaust gas cleaning wash-water piping checks on a scrubber-fitted ferry alongside, to decide which pipe sections to renew at the next docking.

logistics: Antalya has a major international airport with many direct connections, and the team normally flies in directly or connects through Istanbul, then travels by road to the port or the yard. The agent arranges gate passes, terminal safety briefings and launches for the anchorage, while yacht yards and marinas issue their own access, with crew lists and certificates sent ahead. A Turkish visa is needed for Indian passport holders, so we begin the application once a job is likely and keep the validity covering any delay.
vessels: Coasters and small general cargo ships

faqs.q: Can a steel yacht be gauged in a marina or yard at Antalya?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the yard or marina allows the work and the yacht can be accessed safely. On a slipway or hardstand we can measure shell plating, and tanks and keel structure when the owner empties and opens them. We agree a plate map and acceptance criteria with the owner or surveyor beforehand and mark any low readings.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Antalya for a renewal survey on a cargo ship?
faqs.a: No large ocean-going drydock operates here. Merchant ships that need a renewal survey generally go to the Marmara or to a yard elsewhere in the Mediterranean. Readings taken at Antalya during cargo work give the superintendent a measured steel scope before the ship sails for dock.

faqs.q: What can be gauged on a cruise ship during a port call?
faqs.a: Cruise calls are short and tightly programmed, so access is limited to what the ship's technical team releases. Tenders, service craft and certain defined spaces are possible targets. We agree the list in advance, work to the ship's safety rules and report each item as it is finished.

faqs.q: Does the Mediterranean ECA change what you gauge on scrubber-fitted ships?
faqs.a: It makes scrubber piping a priority. Ships burning high-sulphur fuel in the Mediterranean run their exhaust gas cleaning systems constantly, so wash-water and overboard lines are worth checking for thinning. We measure straight runs, bends and the pipe near the hull inlet and discharge, and report the results by line section.
